excerpt_i18n.en: In 2025, the AI community finally shifted from "large model worship" to "application realism." As the parameter competition among foundational models like Baidu's ERNIE, Alibaba's Tongyi, and Tencent's Hunyuan subsided, and the "hundred-model war" evolved into "industry-wide applications," companies suddenly realized that computing power, once considered mere infrastructure, had become the decisive factor in application deployment. The issue isn't a lack of computing power, but the inability to find "just-right" computing power; it's not insufficient computing power, but wasted resources from "misallocated" computing power; it's not unaffordable computing power, but the cost of "ineffective usage" eroding profits. Oracle's $300 billion computing power deal with OpenAI also signals industry change: this isn't merely "selling computing power" but "ecosystem integration." OpenAI requires Oracle's massive computing clusters to support GPT-5's training and inference, while Oracle secures its computing demand for the next decade by partnering with a leading model company. This reflects two core trends in the global computing power market: first, "computing demand shifting from concentration to explosion." Large model training demands immense computing power (GPT-5 requires 10 times that of GPT-3), while inference for multimodal and Agent applications grows exponentially. For instance, a live-streaming AI controller processing video streams, speech recognition, and audience interactions simultaneously consumes far more inference computing power than ordinary tasks.

excerpt_i18n.en: Lei Feng Network AI Tech Review exclusively learned that MiniMax's Senior Research Director, Zhong Yiran, has left the company, with her next destination not yet publicly disclosed. Public records show Dr. Zhong Yiran earned her Ph.D. from the Australian National University under the supervision of Professor Li Hongdong and Academician Richard Hartley. AI is no longer a standalone algorithm but has become the decision-making engine of IoT systems. The new goal for AIoT computing networks and agent systems is to imbue the physical world with cognitive and autonomous capabilities akin to a nervous system. At the 2025 World Laureates Forum, Kevin Yin, founder and CEO of Terminus Group, was invited to share insights with top global tech leaders on advancing the large-scale implementation of advanced AI technologies and launched a series of AIoT products, including "Heterogeneous Computing Super Nodes" and "New Intelligent Agents." 

Redefining AIoT: From Hybrid Intelligence Computing to Super Intelligent Agents

At the forum, Kevin Yin officially unveiled Terminus Group's upgraded corporate strategy, focusing on AIoT technology with computing power (AIoT Infra) and intelligent agents (AIoT Agent) as the two core business areas to accelerate the large-scale deployment of AI. Computing power serves as the foundational support, providing high-performance computational resources for top-level intelligent agents, while the agents enhance the utilization and energy efficiency of cluster resources through their "perception-decision-execution" closed loop, fostering iterative improvements in computing infrastructure and creating a positive feedback cycle.

Kevin Yin also detailed the product architecture and model of Terminus Group's computing power (AIoT Infra) business, which utilizes a cluster of heterogeneous chip hardware and two software platforms—the spatial intelligence base TacOS and the hybrid inference engine HICE—to build a hybrid intelligence computing cloud. This setup offers standardized, stable inference services and computing power leasing operations to the industry, establishing a TaaS (Token as a Service) business model.

En el Foro Mundial de Científicos Líderes 2025, Ai Yu, fundador y CEO de Telstra, fue invitado a compartir logros exploratorios en la implementación a gran escala de tecnologías avanzadas de IA junto con líderes globales de la tecnología, y presentó productos de la serie AIoT como "nodos superiores de computación heterogénea" y "nuevos agentes inteligentes". Redefiniendo AIoT: de la computación inteligente híbrida al superagente inteligente. Durante el foro, Ai Yu lanzó oficialmente la estrategia empresarial actualizada de Telstra, centrada en AIoT.
